It features advanced AI-powered capabilities, including inline suggestions, chat assistance, and autonomous agentic workflows that can plan and execute coding tasks.
keyFeatures: AI-powered agentic workflows for task automation and code generation
Multi-model support with Copilot, Claude, and Codex harnesses
Integrated terminal, debugger, and version control
Extensive marketplace for language support and tool plugins
Cross-interface session continuity via Agent Host Protocol
bestFor: Developers requiring a versatile, fast, and customizable editor for full-cycle development from local coding to cloud deployment.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a full-featured IDE for complex enterprise workflows where a more specialized or heavy-duty IDE environment may be preferred.
recentUpdates: The 1.144 release (October 2026) introduced Agent Host for session continuity, Copilot Fusion for multi-model orchestration, computer use capabilities for agents, and a new direct-edit Markdown editor.
verdict: Visual Studio Code remains the industry-leading editor, now evolving into a sophisticated AI-native platform that bridges local development with autonomous cloud-based agents.

name: Xcode
pricingDetail: The software is free to download. Optional Xcode Cloud compute hours are included with an Apple Developer Program membership (25 hours/month), with additional paid tiers ranging from US$49.99/month for 100 hours to US$3,999/month for 10,000 hours.
description: Xcode is Apple's integrated development environment (IDE) for building, testing, and distributing apps across all Apple platforms. It features advanced coding intelligence, including support for agentic workflows and large language models, alongside professional debugging, profiling, and continuous integration tools.
keyFeatures: Agentic coding support via Model Context Protocol
Integrated cloud-based CI/CD with Xcode Cloud
Predictive code completion and AI-powered coding assistants
Device Hub for managing physical devices and simulators
Advanced Instruments for performance profiling and debugging
bestFor: Developers building native applications for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, and visionOS.
notIdealFor: Developers working on non-Apple platforms, as Xcode is exclusive to the macOS environment.
recentUpdates: Xcode 27 introduced enhanced coding agents, Device Hub for unified device management, and performance testing improvements. Previously, Xcode 26.3 added agentic coding capabilities and permissions management, while Xcode 26 integrated ChatGPT and support for diverse LLM providers.
verdict: Xcode is the essential, industry-standard IDE for the Apple ecosystem, now significantly modernized with robust agentic AI capabilities that automate complex development tasks.

name: JetBrains IDEs
pricingDetail: Includes an AI Free tier with limited cloud credits and unlimited code completion/local models, plus paid AI Pro ($20/month) and AI Ultimate ($60/month) tiers offering higher monthly quotas of AI credits. Enterprise options are available for organizations.
description: JetBrains IDEs provide integrated AI features and support for third-party coding agents to assist with code generation, refactoring, and project-wide analysis. The platform includes native AI Assistant capabilities and the newly introduced JetBrains Air, which allows developers to run and manage various AI agents directly within their coding environment.
keyFeatures: AI-powered code completion and next edit suggestions
JetBrains Air for running and managing multiple AI agents
Context-aware AI chat with support for various LLMs
Integration with deterministic IDE tools for code validation and debugging
Support for local AI models via Ollama or LM Studio
bestFor: Developers who want to combine powerful AI-driven coding assistance with robust IDE capabilities like debugging, profiling, and database management.
notIdealFor: Users who prefer lightweight text editors over full-featured IDEs or those who operate in highly restricted environments where IDE plugins are prohibited.
recentUpdates: As of October 2026, JetBrains launched the Early Access Program for JetBrains Air, an agentic-focused interface for IDEs available via plugin or 2026.3 EAP builds. Previous 2025 releases introduced a unified AI subscription model, the AI Free tier, and the public launch of the Junie coding agent.
verdict: A comprehensive, high-utility development platform that successfully bridges the gap between modern AI agent autonomy and traditional, professional-grade IDE code intelligence.

name: Visual Studio
pricingDetail: Visual Studio Community is free for individual developers, open-source contributors, academic research, and classroom learning, as well as small non-enterprise organizations. Visual Studio Professional and Enterprise are available via paid subscriptions, with Professional starting at $99.99/mo and Enterprise reaching higher tiers depending on licensing. GitHub Copilot features within the IDE have a free tier (with usage limits) and various paid tiers for individuals (starting at $10/mo) and organizations.
description: Visual Studio is a comprehensive, AI-powered Integrated Development Environment (IDE) designed for building complex applications across Windows, web, cloud, and mobile platforms. It integrates deeply with.NET, C++, and Azure, providing advanced debugging, testing, and collaboration tools alongside GitHub Copilot for AI-assisted coding.
keyFeatures: AI-powered coding assistance via GitHub Copilot (Agent mode, Chat, and code completion)
Advanced debugging, diagnostics, and profiling tools
Comprehensive testing suite including live unit testing and test isolation
Deep Azure integration for cloud-native deployment and management
Extensive ecosystem with support for C#, C++, Python,.NET, and thousands of extensions
bestFor: .NET and C++ developers building complex, scalable applications for Windows, cloud, or cross-platform environments who require a full-featured IDE with robust debugging and AI assistance.
notIdealFor: Developers seeking a lightweight, cross-platform code editor for simple scripts or front-end web development; these users may prefer the standalone Visual Studio Code editor instead.
recentUpdates: As of September 2026, Visual Studio features Agent mode for GitHub Copilot, enabling automated planning, testing, and error fixing. Earlier in 2026, the Visual Studio 2026 Insiders program introduced enhanced support for.NET 10, C# 14, and improved Git/CI/CD workflows.
verdict: Visual Studio remains the premier enterprise-grade IDE for the Microsoft ecosystem, now significantly augmented by deeply integrated AI agent workflows that streamline the entire development lifecycle.

name: Copperhead
pricingDetail: The CLI is free and open-source (Apache-2.0). Paid plans include Cloud ($49/user/month), Team ($49/user/month + $199/month platform fee), and custom Enterprise annual licenses.
description: Copperhead is an open-source AI agent designed to automate the creation, documentation, and verification of printed circuit boards (PCBs). It operates directly on KiCad repositories, ensuring that changes remain synchronized across schematics, layouts, and design documentation.
keyFeatures: Surgical edits to KiCad files with git-backed rollbacks
Automated ERC and DRC verification via kicad-cli
Drift detection between documentation and design files
Budget and constraint enforcement during the design process
Pipeline support from product brief to manufacturing files
bestFor: Hardware engineers who want to automate design tasks, sync documentation with schematic changes, and maintain consistency in KiCad repositories.
notIdealFor: Users who require proprietary EDA tools, as Copperhead exclusively supports KiCad; it is also not a replacement for human engineering judgment.
recentUpdates: The project released its public documentation and saw significant traction following a Hacker News launch in September 2026.
verdict: A powerful, developer-centric tool for hardware teams that treats PCB design like code, enforcing strict synchronization and verification to prevent costly design drift.

name: NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR)
pricingDetail: The software is free and open-source.
description: NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR) is a local inference tool that connects multiple computers on your network into a single cluster to distribute AI inference workloads. It proxies API requests to available nodes, allowing users to scale local compute capacity for concurrent tasks without modifying their existing AI applications.
keyFeatures: Workload-aware routing for independent inference requests
Support for Ollama, LM Studio, and llama.cpp engines
Mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption for inter-node communication
Compatibility with OpenAI and Anthropic Messages API formats
Unified management via desktop and terminal interfaces
bestFor: Multi-agent AI workflows and concurrent inference tasks that benefit from distributing parallel requests across multiple local machines.
notIdealFor: Large models requiring pooled GPU memory, requests that must span multiple GPUs, or applications requiring cloud-based inference.
recentUpdates: Version 1.0.0 (released October 2026) added native llama.cpp support, RTX Spark hardware validation, and improved the terminal interface with a dedicated Jobs tab.
verdict: An excellent tool for power users looking to maximize idle local compute for parallel AI tasks, provided they have multiple compatible machines on a trusted network.

name: WebLLM
pricingDetail: WebLLM is an open-source project licensed under Apache-2.0, available as a free npm package and for direct use via CDN.
description: WebLLM is a high-performance, in-browser language model inference engine that leverages WebGPU and WebAssembly for local hardware acceleration. It enables private, serverless AI execution directly within web browsers, maintaining full compatibility with the OpenAI API for seamless integration.
keyFeatures: In-browser hardware-accelerated inference via WebGPU
Full compatibility with OpenAI API
Structured JSON generation and custom schema support
Native support for diverse models like Llama, Phi, Gemma, and Qwen
Web Worker and Service Worker support for background execution
bestFor: Developers building privacy-first web applications, in-browser AI assistants, or Chrome extensions that require local LLM execution without server-side infrastructure.
notIdealFor: Applications requiring massive-scale models that exceed local browser VRAM or environments where users lack WebGPU-supported browsers.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.87 (October 2026) upgraded the web runtime, updated model binaries to v0_2_87, improved Gemma 4 performance, and resolved issues with KV cache and JSON schema generation. Version 0.2.86 added Gemma 4 E2B models with audio/text input and improved vision library support.
verdict: A robust, high-performance solution for running LLMs locally in the browser, ideal for privacy-focused and zero-server architecture projects.

name: Magnitude
pricingDetail: Magnitude is free, open-source software distributed under the Apache 2.0 license with no token costs, paid editions, or managed service tiers.
description: Magnitude is an open-source inference engine that automatically tunes its kernels to your specific hardware to achieve high-performance local model execution. It functions as a desktop application and CLI tool that optimizes model inference specifically for local coding agents.
keyFeatures: On-device kernel tuning for hardware-specific optimization
Built-in speculative decoding with optimized drafters
Dynamic memory allocation and quantized KV cache
One-click integration with popular coding agents
Support for Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, and CPU inference
bestFor: Developers and power users running local coding agents on Apple Silicon or NVIDIA hardware who require high-performance, low-latency inference.
notIdealFor: Users requiring models outside the curated catalog, those using older hardware generations, or platform engineers needing flexible, container-native headless deployments.
recentUpdates: The catalog data was updated on 2026-10-14, following the release of engine v3, with a v4 rewrite currently in progress.
verdict: Magnitude is an architecturally sophisticated inference engine that justifies its performance claims through real-time kernel compilation, though it currently suits a specific set of supported hardware and model families rather than general-purpose GGUF execution.

name: text-to-cad
pricingDetail: This is a free, open-source tool with no paid tiers, subscriptions, or per-generation costs.
description: text-to-cad is an open-source library of agent skills that enables AI coding assistants to generate and inspect CAD models locally. It uses Python scripts and the build123d library to create manufacturing-ready files like STEP, DXF, and G-code directly on your machine.
keyFeatures: Generates CAD geometry as Python scripts with STEP, STL, 3MF, and GLB exports
Performs DFM and DfAM checks for sheet metal, CNC, and 3D printing
Automates robotic structure files including URDF, SRDF, and SDF
Produces dimensioned PDF engineering drawings and 2D DXF layouts
Directly integrates with fabrication services like SendCutSend and Bambu Lab printers
bestFor: Rapid prototyping, creating custom brackets or fixtures, robotics development using URDF, and preparing manufacturable files from AI prompts.
notIdealFor: Regulated engineering industries requiring strict standards compliance, complex multi-part assemblies with persistent parametric constraints, or FEA-validated designs.
recentUpdates: Recent releases in October 2026 (v0.7.19 through v0.7.21) focused on fixing Windows mesh export issues, refining telemetry, and addressing crash triggers during STEP file operations.
verdict: An efficient productivity multiplier for developers and makers comfortable with command-line tools who need a direct bridge between text prompts and physical manufacturing files without the overhead of cloud-based CAD.

name: nanochat
pricingDetail: nanochat is free and open-source under the MIT license. The only cost is GPU compute: the reference GPT-2-grade speedrun takes about 2 hours on an 8xH100 node (roughly $48 at ~$3 per GPU-hour, or closer to $15 on spot instances), while small experiments can run on a single GPU, CPU or Apple Silicon.
description: nanochat is Andrej Karpathy's minimal, hackable harness for training a ChatGPT-style LLM from scratch on a single GPU node. It covers the full pipeline (tokenization, pretraining, supervised finetuning, reinforcement learning, evaluation and inference) in a small PyTorch codebase, and you can talk to the resulting model over a CLI or web UI.
keyFeatures: End-to-end pipeline: tokenizer, pretraining, SFT, RL, evaluation and KV-cache inference in one small codebase
Single --depth dial that derives width, heads, learning rates, training horizon and weight decay for compute-optimal models
runs/speedrun.sh trains a GPT-2-grade model in about 2 hours on an 8xH100 node
Public time-to-GPT-2 leaderboard measured by the DCLM CORE score
Built-in evals (CORE, ARC, GSM8K, HumanEval, MMLU), a Python tool-use sandbox and CPU/MPS support for small runs
bestFor: Developers, researchers and students who want to understand or experiment with every stage of LLM training using a readable codebase and a modest GPU budget.
notIdealFor: Anyone wanting a production-quality assistant or coding model: the resulting models are small and hallucinate freely, and serious runs need multi-GPU H100 or A100 hardware.
recentUpdates: The 2026 work focused on pretraining speed: the time-to-GPT-2 record fell from about 3.04 hours (January) to 1.65 hours (March) through fp8, larger batches, the NVIDIA ClimbMix dataset and agent-driven autoresearch rounds. July 2026 commits added inference benchmarking (scripts/infer_bench.py), tests, a unified optimizer implementation and a hardened execution sandbox.
verdict: The clearest hands-on reference for how a modern chat LLM is built end to end, best used as a learning and research harness rather than a model to deploy.

name: colibri
pricingDetail: colibri is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license with no paid tiers; the project accepts optional donations. You only need your own hardware (8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB or more recommended, plus disk space for model weights).
description: colibri is a pure-C inference engine that runs very large mixture-of-experts open models on ordinary computers by keeping the always-active weights in RAM and streaming experts from disk as the model needs them. A one-step setup recommends a model for your machine, builds or downloads the engine and serves OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints that coding agents can use.
keyFeatures: Expert streaming from disk so hundreds-of-billions-parameter MoE models run in modest RAM
CPU, Vulkan and CUDA backends with an optional GPU
Runs published GGUF files as-is, from IQ1_S to Q8_0, F16, BF16 and MXFP4
OpenAI-compatible /v1 and Anthropic-compatible endpoints for coding agents
One-step start-here setup with hardware profiling, model recommendation, resumable downloads and a coli ui dashboard
bestFor: Developers who want to run frontier-scale open MoE models such as GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi or Qwen locally for private coding-agent work without buying datacenter GPUs.
notIdealFor: Latency-sensitive production serving or dense models, since streaming experts from disk trades speed for memory and throughput depends heavily on disk and RAM bandwidth.
recentUpdates: v2.1.0 (October 31, 2026) added native GGUF support on every engine, Mistral-Large-4, Muse Spark Open, Flint and LFM3-VL, CUDA device chains, speculative decoding via MTP heads, 262k-token contexts for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and a new chat UI; v2.0.0 shipped October 6, 2026.
verdict: An impressively compact way to run giant open MoE models on consumer hardware, with agent-ready APIs that make it a practical local backend for coding agents if you can accept disk-bound speeds.

name: FreeToken
pricingDetail: FreeToken is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license, including the Windows and Linux desktop app. There are no paid tiers; you supply your own NVIDIA RTX 30, 40 or 50 series GPU and host memory.
description: FreeToken is an edge-native mixture-of-experts serving engine for running frontier-scale open-weight models on personal hardware. It treats GPUs, CPUs, host memory and interconnects as one elastic inference platform and exposes Anthropic- and OpenAI-compatible APIs for coding and tool-calling agents.
keyFeatures: Bandwidth-adaptive CPU-GPU co-execution with double-buffered prefill streaming and global LRU expert caching
Semantic anchor checkpoints so agentic context edits avoid recomputing KV and recurrent state
Runtime VRAM rebalancing between expert cache and KV memory without restarts
Support for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.6, GLM-5.2, gpt-oss and GGUF checkpoints in MXFP4, NVFP4, FP8 and BF16
Anthropic- and OpenAI-compatible APIs for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and OpenClaw, via a desktop app or uv/pip CLI
bestFor: Developers with an NVIDIA gaming or workstation GPU who want to run 100B-300B-class open MoE models locally as a fast backend for coding agents.
notIdealFor: Apple Silicon, AMD or CPU-only users, and anyone who needs a mature, long-stable serving stack, since the project targets NVIDIA RTX hardware and is at version 0.2.
recentUpdates: v0.2.0 (October 21, 2026) and v0.2.1 (October 26, 2026) added image input from llama.cpp mmproj files, DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3-VL GGUF architectures, Flint support and host-RAM embedding tables; a November 2, 2026 commit added gpt-oss GGUF serving. The accompanying arXiv paper (2608.16157) describes the design.
verdict: A research-backed, fast-moving local MoE server that brings datacenter-style serving techniques to consumer NVIDIA GPUs and is a strong local backend for agent workloads.

name: Floorplan
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (MIT). Runs on your existing Claude Code or Codex plan with no API keys and no paid tier.
description: Open-source Claude Code and Codex plugin that has your coding agent read a codebase (one repo or several) and draw a local, interactive, plain-English map of its parts, files, endpoints, screens and outside services, with an Ask bar, recent-change highlights and a security-focused Health check.
keyFeatures: Zoomable map from whole app down to files and endpoints
Matches frontend web requests to server endpoints, even across repos
Ask the map: answers with a mini-map and step-by-step walkthrough
Recent work view highlights what the agent just changed and why
Health check for leaked keys, open Supabase/Firebase rules, fakeable Stripe webhooks and unauthenticated endpoints
Blueprints that plan an unbuilt app from a PRD or spec
Runs locally with zero dependencies; exports a single HTML file
bestFor: Builders and teams using Claude Code or Codex who want a plain-English architecture map of an AI-built app, faster onboarding, and a quick check for common security mistakes.
notIdealFor: Developers who need function-level knowledge graphs of very large codebases, formal security audits, or support for agents other than Claude Code and Codex.
recentUpdates: v0.6.3 (Nov 2, 2026) added route-table endpoints, full Fastify and Django endpoint prefixes and a parsing fix; v0.6.0-0.6.2 added AI-app Health checks and far fewer false alarms with a Not a problem button.
verdict: A fast-moving, privacy-friendly way to see how an agent-built app fits together; its Health check is a useful first pass, not an audit, and it is limited to Claude Code and Codex for now.

name: TokenEconomizer
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (Apache-2.0). Needs no API key of its own; model usage, including the plugin's own model calls, is billed to the agent plan or key you already use.
description: Open-source cost-control plugin from Microsoft Research and UC Berkeley that learns across a repository's sessions to cut what coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and Pi spend, without changing the agent's model or code.
keyFeatures: Micro-skills: repo facts learned from repeated evidence are injected at session start
Tool pruning removes tools that go unused, through the agent's own settings
Failure-loop intervention spots repeated errors and nudges the agent to try another way
Every action reversible: contradicted facts are dropped and pruned tools can be restored
Plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and Pi; Cursor Agent, opencode and Hermes Agent experimental
Cost counted with cache pricing, including the plugin's own model calls
Reproducible SWE-Bench and Web-Bench experiments in the repo
bestFor: Developers and teams who run the same coding agent on the same repositories every day and want lower token bills without switching agents or models.
notIdealFor: One-off sessions in new repositories (savings accrue over repeated sessions), Windows users of the Cursor adapter, or anyone on agent versions outside the supported ranges.
recentUpdates: Released Oct 2026 with the arXiv paper (2610.22732); Nov 4, 2026 commits reduced loop-guard false alarms so a productive turn is not treated as a loop and documented model-call costs.
verdict: A credible, research-backed way to trim 18-31% off coding-agent costs on familiar repos; install is still clone-based and pinned to specific agent versions, so expect some upkeep.

name: Agent Autoloop
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (MIT). Runs locally on your machine with the CLI agents you already have; model usage is billed to your own provider account.
description: Open-source local hub that turns command-line coding agents into a background loop: it takes work from webhooks, issue polling, cron rules or an HTTP API, dispatches it to Claude Code, Codex, ACP agents or any CLI, and only sends you a decision card when your call is needed.
keyFeatures: Zero-dependency, event-sourced SQLite kernel (about 1,650 lines)
Agents: Claude Code, Codex, ACP, DeepSeek Harness or any prompt-in/reply-out CLI
Events from GitHub/GitLab webhooks, issue polling, cron rules and an HTTP API
Decision cards via desktop notifications, Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, Slack or Discord
Zero-cost wait: no agent process or tokens while waiting for your answer, then the session resumes
Hop circuit breaker and `agent-autoloop why` run histories
`deliver` label pipeline: review, wait for CI, merge, wait for deploy, verify
bestFor: Developers on macOS or Linux who want their existing Claude Code or Codex setup to pick up issues, alerts and scheduled chores in the background with human approval only when needed.
notIdealFor: Windows users (native support pending; WSL2 only), teams wanting a hosted dashboard, or users who need English CLI output and docs today.
recentUpdates: v1.3.0 through v1.4.1 shipped on Nov 5, 2026, two days after the Nov 3 launch, with kernel and plugin cleanups; native Windows support is promised in issue #17.
verdict: A thoughtfully engineered, fast-growing way to run CLI agents unattended with human-in-the-loop cards; very new and Chinese-first, so expect rough edges for English-speaking users.

name: Harp
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (AGPL-3.0). Harp adds no servers of its own; upstream Warp AI and cloud features follow Warp's own terms.
description: Open-source, unofficial macOS fork of the Warp terminal that replaces the tab bar with a sidebar for running many Claude Code and Codex agents side by side, showing which session is working, waiting for you or done.
keyFeatures: Sidebar rows show working, needs-you, done and background-work states per agent
Bundled Claude Code status plugin, with nothing installed into ~/.claude
Codex status read from the agent's terminal title and session logs
Named tab groups that persist through tmux integration
Limit rings for Claude and Codex plan usage, extensible via a JSON file
Signed DMG with background self-updates from GitHub releases
Runs next to Warp with its own bundle id and ~/.harp settings
bestFor: macOS developers who already like Warp and juggle several Claude Code or Codex sessions, wanting to see at a glance which agent needs attention.
notIdealFor: Linux or Windows users, people who want an officially supported Warp build, or agents other than Claude Code and Codex.
recentUpdates: v0.1.7 and v0.1.8 (Oct 29, 2026) turned agent status on out of the box for Claude Code and Codex and show when Codex is waiting on you.
verdict: A focused, polished take on agent-aware tabs for Warp fans on macOS; young and single-maintainer, so treat it as an early unofficial fork.

name: Gauge
pricingDetail: CLI is free and open-source (MIT) and the local loop needs no Gauge account; agent usage is billed to your own provider or subscription. Hosted Gauge runs on a Gauge workspace with credits.
description: Open-source CLI that measures and improves agent experience: it runs real coding agents against your Skills, CLIs, SDKs, MCP servers or docs in sandboxed sessions, captures where they get stuck, and lets your own coding agent test fixes before you publish.
keyFeatures: Runs Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode in fresh Docker sessions
Normalizes agent events into consistent transcripts and structured findings
Saved evals, preference prompts and shared Markdown cases for CI
Tests unreleased CLI/SDK tarballs and working-tree Skills before publishing
Issue tracking with fix, mute, reopen and recheck commands
`gauge watch` live view of past and running sessions
Hosted mode adds automatic analysis, authenticated MCP/API and docs testing
bestFor: Teams shipping CLIs, SDKs, MCP servers, Skills or docs who want evidence of how coding agents actually use them and a repeatable loop to fix friction.
notIdealFor: Developers looking for a coding assistant to write their own app code, or environments without Docker and Node.js 22.13+.
recentUpdates: v0.28.0 (Nov 4, 2026) added hosted `--cli-rules` to stub or redirect CLI commands per run; v0.27.0 (Nov 2) added hosted setup/teardown scripts, issue fix/mute/recheck commands and `gauge watch`.
verdict: A distinctive, fast-shipping eval loop for agent-facing products; still early with a small community, and the richer analysis lives in the paid hosted tier.

name: Kandev
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (AGPL-3.0); self-host it locally or on your own servers. Agent usage is billed to your own provider subscriptions or API keys.
description: Open-source, self-hostable kanban board and development environment that runs many coding agents in parallel, chains them into multi-step workflows with review gates, and puts their output in one IDE-like review workspace.
keyFeatures: Kanban and pipeline views with drag-and-drop tasks and workflow automation
20+ agents via ACP or TUI passthrough: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Amp, OpenCode, Cursor, Devin, Kiro, Grok and more
Agentic workflows that mix agents per step, e.g. plan, implement and review
Integrated workspace with file tree, LSP editor, terminal, browser preview and git changes
Git worktree isolation per task, including multi-repository tasks
Local, Docker, Kubernetes, SSH and sprites.dev executors
Schedule and webhook automations plus GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Sentry and Azure DevOps integrations
bestFor: Power users and teams who run several coding agents at once and want a self-hosted board with review gates and per-task worktrees instead of juggling terminal tabs.
notIdealFor: Developers who want a single hosted agent with no setup, or users who need signed desktop installers today.
recentUpdates: v0.99.0 (Nov 5, 2026) and v0.99.1 (Nov 6) continued near-daily releases, adding Copilot compaction counts from native events and continuing failed turns after capacity and command errors; a plugin SDK (pluginsdk/v0.1.0) shipped on Nov 5.
verdict: One of the most complete open-source agent orchestration boards, shipping fast with a broad agent and executor matrix; pre-1.0 and its desktop builds are still unsigned.

name: Stroq
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (Apache-2.0). Runs locally via `npx @stroq/cli` with no account and no telemetry.
description: Open-source local security layer for AI coding agents that audits past Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions for injected commands and leaked keys, and installs pre-tool-call hooks that block or question risky actions next time.
keyFeatures: `stroq` card summarizing 30 days of agent sessions: commands that came from text the agent read and keys that left the machine
`stroq sent` traces where each known credential went, printing key names, never values
`stroq replay` checks past sessions against the policy without installing hooks
Native hooks for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot CLI, Windsurf and Antigravity, plus an OpenClaw plugin and stdio MCP proxy
Denies curl-pipe-to-shell and secret-carrying outbound calls; asks when a command repeats text the agent read
Local console on 127.0.0.1 with Check, Live, Agents, Rules and Skills & MCP screens
`stroq attack` replays 36 known attacks against your policy in a sandbox
bestFor: Developers running Claude Code, Codex or Cursor locally who want to see whether prompt-injected content drove their agent's commands and to guard future sessions without a cloud service.
notIdealFor: Teams needing a true sandbox or centrally managed enterprise policy; matching is text-level and only sees what each agent's hooks expose.
recentUpdates: v0.30.0 (Nov 5, 2026) added the `stroq` session card, detection of tasks slipped into data the agent reads, and a five-screen console; it was posted to Hacker News as a Show HN the same day.
verdict: A thoughtful, privacy-first audit and guard for agent sessions with clear documented limits; young and single-maintainer, but shipping weekly.

name: Figma Console MCP
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (MIT). Requires a Figma account and personal access token; Remote SSE and Cloud Mode are hosted by Southleft at no charge.
description: Open-source, design-system-focused MCP server that connects Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other AI clients to Figma in both directions: extracting tokens and components, writing designs, and running design-code parity and accessibility checks.
keyFeatures: Up to 130 tools locally via `npx -y figma-console-mcp@latest` (105 in Cloud Mode)
Design creation and editing through a Figma Desktop Bridge plugin
Bidirectional token sync with DTCG JSON and nine other formats
Deterministic design-code parity, WCAG accessibility and design-system health audits
Codebase-to-design-system extraction into DTCG tokens with provenance
Version history diffs, changelogs and component docs
Remote SSE (read-only) and Cloud Mode for web clients such as Claude.ai, v0 and Replit
bestFor: Design engineers and front-end teams who want coding agents to read and write their Figma design system and keep code and design in sync.
notIdealFor: Teams not using Figma, or users who want write access without installing Figma Desktop and its bridge plugin.
recentUpdates: v1.46.0 (Oct 29, 2026) added shader tools, one-call auto layout and CSS-style grid layout, OKLCH and Display P3 colors, and text wrap and variable-font axes; v1.45 added Motion animation and video export.
verdict: The most feature-rich open-source Figma MCP for agent-driven design-system work, actively maintained by an agency; the full tool set depends on the desktop bridge plugin.

name: unslop
pricingDetail: Free and open (CC-BY-4.0) for any use, including commercial, with attribution. A paid done-for-you service from the author is offered separately.
description: Agent skill for Claude Code and Codex that audits vibecoded, AI-looking UI for slop and redesigns it pass by pass into an interface with its own character, in whatever stack the screen is built with.
keyFeatures: `/unslop` in Claude Code and `$unslop` in Codex, with a one-line Codex skill-installer install
Audit that lists every sign of slop and where it lives
Proposes a design direction from your product before editing
Ordered passes: spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion
Works with Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML/CSS, or a live site via Playwright snapshot
Optional hero visuals through an image MCP server, after asking
Sub-10-second story video of the screen unslopping itself (Playwright and ffmpeg)
bestFor: Developers shipping agent-built dashboards, apps or landing pages who want a designer-style redline pass without leaving Claude Code or Codex.
notIdealFor: Teams with an established design system and designers, or agents other than Claude Code and Codex.
recentUpdates: Released at the end of October 2026; on Nov 1, 2026 it added Codex support with a one-line skill-installer install and fixes for Playwright snapshot setup and responsive images.
verdict: A popular, opinionated design-cleanup skill that fills a real gap in agent-built UIs; very new and single-author, so results depend on the agent following a long skill.

name: Rivet
pricingDetail: Open-source (Apache-2.0) and free to run locally or self-host, with S3 as the only dependency. Rivet Cloud (fully managed dedicated clusters on AWS or GCP) and BYOC (control plane in your own VPC, managed by Rivet) are managed options; see rivet.dev for their pricing.
description: Open-source orchestrator for agentic workloads built on Rivet Actors: long-lived processes with in-memory state, a per-Actor SQLite database on S3, WebSockets and scheduling, so every agent, user, session or tenant gets its own durable process that hibernates when idle.
keyFeatures: Rivet Actors with in-memory state, per-Actor SQLite on S3, WebSockets and cron scheduling
Hibernates idle Actors and wakes them on the next request with state intact
Durable Agents library and replaying Workflows built on Actors
agentOS sandboxing (V8 and WebAssembly) for code an agent writes, with network and filesystem controls
End-to-end typed TypeScript clients (`rivetkit`), React hooks, scoped JWTs and OpenTelemetry
`npx skills add rivet-dev/skills` lets Claude Code, Cursor or Codex scaffold a Rivet project
Self-host on Docker, Kubernetes or a VM, or use Rivet Cloud or BYOC
bestFor: Teams building production AI agents or multiplayer agent apps that need durable per-agent state, realtime connections and cheap idle capacity without running a VM per agent.
notIdealFor: Developers looking for a ready-made coding assistant, or teams whose agents need a full Linux VM for every session regardless of workload.
recentUpdates: v3.0.6 was released on Nov 6, 2026, a day after v3.0.5; Rivet launched on Hacker News as a Launch HN (YC W23) on Nov 5, 2026, pitching agent orchestration on S3.
verdict: A well-engineered, actively shipped runtime that moves the agent loop out of the sandbox; strongest for TypeScript teams building agent products, less relevant if you only consume coding agents.

name: AI-DLC
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (MIT-0). Model usage is billed through whichever harness and provider you already use (for example Claude Code, Kiro, Codex or Amazon Bedrock).
description: AI-Driven Development Life Cycle from AWS Labs: a harness-neutral workflow engine that turns coding agents into structured, auditable software delivery, with phases, stages, specialist agents, approval gates and persistent project state.
keyFeatures: One core that runs natively in Claude Code, Kiro IDE and Kiro CLI, Codex CLI, Cursor, opencode and GitHub Copilot
Native `aidlc` command installed via `install.sh` or `install.ps1`; `aidlc config --harness <name>` and `aidlc doctor`
5 phases and 33 stages from initialization through operation
14 agents: 11 domain experts, 2 reviewers and an adaptive composer
11 workflow profiles covering features, bug fixes, infrastructure, security, proofs of concept and enterprise delivery
Human approval gates with source-bound review evidence
Audit trail, persistent state, team knowledge and learned rules
bestFor: Teams that want a repeatable, reviewable delivery process around AI coding agents across several harnesses, especially in AWS or Kiro environments.
notIdealFor: Quick one-off edits or solo prototyping where approval gates and a staged lifecycle add more ceremony than value.
recentUpdates: v2.11.3 (Nov 4, 2026) ships a native `aidlc` built with Bun 1.4.4, team Units support end to end and OpenCode 2 support; 2.11.4 preview builds followed on Nov 5 and Nov 6, adding the `kiro-v2` harness name for Kiro CLI (V2).
verdict: A thorough, fast-moving spec-and-gates methodology from AWS that works across the major coding agents; heavier than lightweight spec tools, but strong on auditability.

name: Google Agent Skills
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (Apache-2.0). Skills are Markdown instructions; using the Google Cloud or other Google products they target is billed by those products.
description: Google's official library of Agent Skills (SKILL.md) for Google products and technologies, led by Google Cloud, installable into coding agents with one command and bundled with Google product plugins (skills plus MCP servers) for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLI.
keyFeatures: Install with `npx skills add google/skills`, choosing skills, target agents and scope
Google Cloud recipes for auth, onboarding and foundation setup
Multi-product solution skills such as building and deploying agents, RAG on GKE and AlloyDB, and GKE inference migration
Agent Platform skills for inference, tuning, evals, model registry and prompt management
Infrastructure, databases, security, hosting, Ads and Well-Architected Framework skills
Plugin marketplace for Claude Code (`claude plugin marketplace add google/skills`), Codex and Antigravity CLI
Links sibling packs for Android, Dart, Flutter, Firestore, ADK and Google Maps
bestFor: Developers using Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Antigravity to build on Google Cloud who want agents to follow current, official Google guidance.
notIdealFor: Teams that do not use Google Cloud or other Google products, since most skills target that stack.
recentUpdates: Commits landed daily in early November 2026, including a new pathways-workload skill for debugging Pathways workloads on Cloud (Nov 6) and an updated Antigravity agent ID (Nov 7); the repository passed 23,000 GitHub stars.
verdict: The canonical skills pack for agent work on Google Cloud; broad and actively maintained, though its value depends on how much of your stack is Google.

name: mini-swe-agent
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the MIT License; you pay only for the model API calls (via litellm, OpenRouter, Portkey or a local model) and any sandbox infrastructure you run it in.
description: mini-swe-agent is a minimal AI software engineering agent from the team behind SWE-bench and SWE-agent. The agent class is about 100 lines of Python, it uses only bash instead of a custom tool interface, and it keeps a linear message history that is also the trajectory, so it is easy to read, modify and run with any model.
keyFeatures: About 100 lines of Python for the core agent class, built to be hacked on
Bash as the only tool, so no tool-calling API is required and any model works
Model support via litellm, OpenRouter and Portkey, including /completion and /response endpoints
Local, Docker/Podman, Singularity/Apptainer and Bubblewrap execution environments
`mini` CLI for interactive use plus batch runs over SWE-bench and a trajectory browser
Install with `uvx mini-swe-agent`, `pipx run mini-swe-agent` or `pip install mini-swe-agent`
bestFor: Researchers and engineers who want a small, transparent coding agent baseline for benchmarks, fine-tuning or sandboxed batch runs, and developers who want a simple bash-only agent in the terminal.
notIdealFor: Developers who want a polished IDE experience, rich built-in tooling or a managed product with team features.
recentUpdates: mini-swe-agent v2 is the current major version (v2.4.6 released Jul 23, 2026); the README now highlights that it powers Ramp SWE-Bench and serves as an evaluation harness for the DeepSWE benchmark, and the original SWE-agent is in maintenance mode with mini-swe-agent as its successor.
verdict: The reference minimal coding agent: tiny, model agnostic and benchmark proven, best as a hackable baseline rather than a full daily driver.

name: Agent Substrate
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the Apache License 2.0; you pay for your own Kubernetes cluster, compute, storage and model usage.
description: Agent Substrate is a security-hardened, zero-trust runtime for running large numbers of sandboxed agents on standard Kubernetes. It maps many stateful actors onto a small pool of warm workers, snapshots idle actors out of memory and restores them on request, and keeps credentials outside the sandbox. Google donated it to the CNCF alongside gVisor in November 2026.
keyFeatures: Every actor runs in a gVisor or microVM sandbox with segregated compute, network and storage
Short-lived per-actor SPIFFE identity and default-deny networking
Egress gateway (`atenet-egress`) injects credentials outside the sandbox so agents never hold API keys
Snapshots RAM and filesystem state of idle actors and resumes them in under 500 ms
10x to 30x oversubscription of stateful actors onto warm worker pods
Harness agnostic: hosts ADK, LangChain, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and sandboxed MCP servers
Base layer for Google AX (Agent Executor) and kagent
bestFor: Platform teams that need to run many untrusted, mostly idle agents or coding sandboxes on Kubernetes with strong isolation, identity and credential controls.
notIdealFor: Individual developers or small teams without Kubernetes experience who just want to run a coding agent locally.
recentUpdates: v1.0.0 was released on Nov 5, 2026 with a public API and configuration compatibility commitment, and on Nov 6, 2026 Google announced it is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF.
verdict: A serious, production-minded isolation layer for agent fleets; heavy to operate, but one of the strongest open options for running untrusted agents at scale.

name: GSD Core
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the MIT License; it runs inside the coding agent you already use, so your only costs are that agent's subscription or API usage.
description: GSD Core ("Git. Ship. Done.") is a light-weight meta-prompting, context-engineering and spec-driven development system for AI coding agents. It runs each milestone through a Discuss, Plan, Execute, Verify, Ship loop and pushes heavy research, planning and execution into fresh-context subagents to avoid context rot in the main session.
keyFeatures: Five-step phase loop: Discuss, Plan, Execute, Verify, Ship
Heavy work runs in fresh-context subagents, executed in parallel waves
`STATE.md` and `CONTEXT.md` artifacts that survive session boundaries
Verify step walks through what was built and writes fix plans before a phase is done
One installer (`npx @opengsd/gsd-core@latest`) for Claude Code, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, Kimi CLI, Kilo, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf and more
`/gsd-new-project` for greenfield work and `/gsd-onboard` for existing codebases
bestFor: Developers running multi-phase features with a coding agent who want structured planning, verification and clean context without adopting a new IDE.
notIdealFor: Quick one-off edits, or users who want minimal token use, since the subagent-heavy workflow trades extra tokens for quality.
recentUpdates: v1.20.1 was released on Nov 5, 2026, two days after v1.20.0, fixing fork-probe cache handling and installer path rewriting for nested config directories across runtimes.
verdict: A popular, actively shipped spec-driven workflow layer that works across most coding agents; worth trying if context rot is hurting long agent sessions.

name: Capy
pricingDetail: Every plan includes unlimited members, and the plan sets your monthly credits and cloud machine limits. Lite costs $20/mo ($16/mo billed annually) with $20 of credits, and your first 7 days cost $1 with a verified card. Pro costs $100/mo ($80/mo annually) with $105 of credits and adds mobile builds and devices. Max runs from $200 to $1,000/mo in $100 steps with 10% bonus credits. Enterprise is custom and adds SSO/SAML and audit logging. You can bring your own API keys, or a ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot or SuperGrok subscription, on every plan.
description: Capy runs a fleet of cloud coding agents in parallel, taking each task from plan to merged PR. You can start work from the Capy desktop app, the web UI, Slack, Linear, GitHub, triggers or cron. Each agent runs in an isolated cloud VM. Captains coordinate crews of agent threads, and a built-in review agent checks every PR.
keyFeatures: Run hundreds of agents in parallel, each in an isolated cloud VM with snapshots and Docker-in-Docker
Captains (GA in v0.7.0) direct crews of threads that pick up work from built-in Issues
Built-in review agent runs on every PR, and you can create and review PRs inside Capy
Computer use, browser use and annotated videos for end-to-end testing, plus iOS and Android builds tested on cloud phones (Pro and Max plans)
Claude, GPT, Gemini and other models, with bring-your-own API keys or a ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot or SuperGrok subscription
Slack, Linear, GitHub and Sentry integrations, plus scheduled and triggered automations
Dock CLI (`capy dock`) runs threads headless on any macOS, Linux or Windows machine
bestFor: Engineering teams that want to hand off backlogs, migrations, bug triage, PR review and E2E testing to many cloud agents at once, starting work from Slack or Linear.
notIdealFor: Developers who want a free or local-only tool, or who prefer working with one agent inside their editor instead of managing a fleet of cloud agents.
recentUpdates: Capy 0.7.2 (Nov 1, 2026) made the Dock CLI installable on macOS, Linux and Windows. Capy 0.7.0 (Oct 31, 2026) made Captains and Issues GA, added the Dock CLI and added a context breakdown view. On Oct 28, 2026 Capy announced iOS and Android app testing on cloud phones.
verdict: A capable platform for running many cloud agents in parallel, with strong team integrations, model flexibility and unlimited members. Usage is billed in credits, so costs grow with agent activity.

name: Executor
pricingDetail: The CLI, desktop app and self-hosted server are MIT-licensed and free. Executor Cloud is free for up to 3 members with unlimited integrations; Team costs $15 per member per month after a 14-day free trial and adds verified domains; Enterprise is custom and adds self-hosted or dedicated cloud deployment support, SSO/SAML, SCIM, audit logs for every tool call and dedicated support.
description: Executor is an open-source integration layer and tool gateway for AI agents. You connect each account once, and any MCP-compatible agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT and others) reaches those services through one MCP endpoint without seeing the credential. Since v2, integrations are apps: small TypeScript programs that wrap an OpenAPI spec, proxy a remote MCP server or call an API by hand, and can store data, serve a UI and run on schedules or webhooks.
keyFeatures: One MCP endpoint shared by every agent, with credentials attached inside apps so agents never see API keys or OAuth tokens
Apps written in TypeScript that wrap OpenAPI specs, remote MCP servers or hand-written API calls, with stored data, their own UI and background runs
Code mode: agents get `skills` and `execute` tools and run short programs across many apps instead of single tool calls
Per-tool approvals (always, never, or only when input looks risky), answered in the MCP client, through the agent or on a browser page
Versioned deploys with rollback, plus a catalog of ready-made apps and agents that can write and deploy new ones
Hosted Executor Cloud, local CLI and desktop app, or self-hosting in one Docker container with an embedded database
bestFor: Developers and teams who use several coding agents and want one governed place for integrations, credentials and approval policies instead of configuring MCP servers and API keys in every client.
notIdealFor: People who want an agent that does the work itself (Executor runs no AI), or teams that need a visual flow builder like Zapier or n8n rather than automations written as code.
recentUpdates: Executor v2 launched on November 5, 2026, reworking the product around TypeScript apps, `skills` and `execute` code-mode tools and agent-built automations; new sign-ups moved to v2 while v1 users can opt in. Releases continue in the 2.0.0 beta line, with executor@2.0.0-beta.38 published on November 9, 2026.
verdict: A well-designed, actively developed gateway that removes repeated integration and credential setup across agents, with a free open-source local option and simple per-member cloud pricing.

name: Astryx
pricingDetail: Astryx is free and open-source under the MIT license, including the core components, themes, CLI and the hosted MCP server. There are no paid tiers.
description: Astryx is Meta's open-source React and StyleX design system, refined inside Meta for eight years across more than 13,000 apps and released in beta in June 2026. It is built for coding agents as well as people: a CLI writes agent docs into AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md and hands agents templates and component props, and a remote MCP server lets AI tools search and read the documentation directly.
keyFeatures: 150+ accessible React 19 components, ready-to-ship templates, dark mode and token-level theming with CSS custom properties
`npx @astryxdesign/cli init --features agents` generates a component index, behavioural rules and CLI reference for your AI tool
CLI `build`, `template` and `component` commands give agents the closest page template, scaffolding and component props
Remote MCP server at astryx.atmeta.com/mcp with `search` and `get` tools for Claude Code, Cursor, Cline and other MCP clients
`swizzle` ejects a component's full source into your project, and styles can be overridden with Tailwind, CSS modules or plain CSS
bestFor: React teams that build internal tools or apps with coding agents and want a design system the agent can query and follow, so generated UI uses real components and tokens instead of ad hoc markup.
notIdealFor: Projects on React versions before 19, non-React stacks, or teams that need a stable 1.0 API, since Astryx is still in beta with frequent releases.
recentUpdates: Astryx 0.7.11 shipped on November 7, 2026 with touch-aware Popover growth animations, `delay` and `hideDelay` on DropdownMenuSubMenu, a `timezoneID` prop on Timestamp and many accessibility fixes; 0.7.10 shipped on November 6, 2026. The repository passed 19,000 GitHub stars in November 2026.
verdict: A mature, production-tested design system that treats coding agents as first-class users through its CLI and MCP server, making it a strong base for agent-built React UI.

name: llama-modchip
pricingDetail: llama-modchip is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license with no paid tiers. You supply your own hardware: 16 to 32 GB of RAM for 30B MoE models or 64 GB for the 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash build.
description: llama-modchip is a set of ggml/llama.cpp kernel patches, quantization transcoders and runtime tools for running mixture-of-experts models entirely in system RAM on CPUs, with an optional GPU for hybrid runs. Its Fractal-64 quantization fits the 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash into 64 GB of RAM, and KV slot snapshots let coding-agent prompts restore in milliseconds, with a `modchip claude` command that wires Claude Code to the local server.
keyFeatures: Fractal-64 and Fractal-MXFP4 quantization that fits 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash in 64 GB RAM and 30B MoEs in 16 to 32 GB
Cache-tiled SIMD kernel patches for AVX-512, AVX2, ARM64 NEON/SVE and Apple Metal
Self-speculative n-gram drafter and `/dev/shm` KV slot snapshots for fast agent context restore
`modchip` CLI for setup, chat, web HUD, benchmarks, evals, quantization and `modchip claude` to launch Claude Code against the local 256K-context server
Hardware readiness check and a community CPU benchmark leaderboard
bestFor: Developers with a 64 GB desktop or workstation and no large GPU who want to run big open MoE models locally as a private backend for Claude Code and other coding agents.
notIdealFor: Users who want stock llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio compatibility (Fractal-64 GGUFs need the patched binaries) or a mature, multi-maintainer project, since it launched in late October 2026.
recentUpdates: v2.4.0 shipped on November 4, 2026 after v2.2.0 and v2.3.0 on November 2 and 3, 2026; commits on November 9, 2026 added macOS and Windows hardware detection and automatic Fractal-64 GGUF selection. The project reached the Hacker News front page in early November 2026.
verdict: An ambitious CPU-first MoE runtime that makes very large open models usable on ordinary desktops for local agent work, best treated as an experimental fork until its patches settle.

name: Delta
pricingDetail: Personal is free and works with your own API keys or external agents such as Claude Code. Pro costs $10 per month and adds Zed-hosted models with $5 of tokens included each month and usage-based billing beyond that. The account and credits are shared with the Zed editor.
description: Delta is a multiplayer environment for coding with agents and reviewing what they build, made by Zed Industries. Teammates and agents work in one thread, and DeltaDB records every edit together with the conversation behind it on top of your existing git repository, so reviewers can see how code came to be and comment in context.
keyFeatures: Shared threads where several people and agents work and review together in real time
DeltaDB records every edit with its conversation and lets you revert to any edit in a thread
Comments anchored to code lines or messages that stay attached as the work evolves
Desktop apps for macOS, Linux and Windows, a web app and mobile browser access
Beta Delta CLI connects Claude Code sessions to Delta threads
Review subthreads with an isolated copy of the parent thread's worktrees
bestFor: Teams that want agent conversations, code changes and review in one shared place, especially those already using Zed or looking to replace pull-request-centred review with threads.
notIdealFor: Teams that need a stable, finished product or depend on GitHub pull request workflows and CI integrations, since Delta is in public beta and some capabilities are still on the roadmap.
recentUpdates: Delta entered public beta on September 16, 2026, after a private beta that started on August 12, 2026; Zed says it disabled pull requests on Delta's own repository and now builds Delta entirely within Delta. Pricing offers a free Personal plan and a $10 per month Pro plan shared with Zed.
verdict: A thoughtful take on collaborative agent coding that keeps the reasoning behind every change, worth trying for teams already comfortable with Zed, with the caveat that it is still a beta.

name: Boxes.dev
pricingDetail: Trial is free with 20 box-hours per user. Starter costs $19 per seat per month (50 box-hours), Pro $99 per seat per month (300 box-hours) and Max $249 per seat per month (750 box-hours); extra usage is $0.40 per box-hour from prepaid credits. Enterprise is custom. Standard boxes are 4 vCPU and 8 GB RAM, billed by the second, and model usage runs on your own Codex or Claude subscription or API key.
description: Boxes.dev gives every Claude Code or Codex agent its own Linux cloud computer, a devbox cloned from a Template box of your dev environment. You start agents from Slack, Linear, a schedule or the API, and steer them from the desktop app, web, CLI or phone while your laptop is closed.
keyFeatures: One isolated cloud devbox per agent thread, with its own filesystem, services and ports
Template box ported from your local setup by setup agents, with snapshots for new devboxes
Port forwarding to localhost and integrated terminal access
Start agents from Slack, Linear, cron schedules or one API call
Unmodified Claude Code and Codex harnesses using your existing subscription or API key
Idle boxes sleep automatically and sleeping boxes are free
bestFor: Developers and small teams who run several Claude Code or Codex agents in parallel and want each one on a full cloud machine instead of local worktrees.
notIdealFor: Teams that want an agent with its own model and harness, or developers who need agents to run on local hardware or offline.
recentUpdates: Boxes.dev now offers plans from a free 20 box-hour trial to Max at $249 per seat per month, with prepaid credit discounts of up to 10% and help docs covering Template boxes, devbox management and the desktop app.
verdict: A focused, well-designed way to run off-the-shelf coding agents in parallel on real cloud machines, with clear box-hour pricing.

name: Hoplite
pricingDetail: Free plan at $0 with 5 concurrent cloud sessions, sandboxes up to 2 vCPU and 8 GiB, and 5 projects. Team costs $60 per seat per month or $50 per seat per month billed yearly. Enterprise is a custom annual agreement.
description: Hoplite runs cloud coding agents that take a task from request to reviewed code. Each thread works in an isolated sandbox with your repository, runs tests, drives a browser against the app preview and opens a GitHub pull request, then keeps iterating in the same thread as review feedback arrives.
keyFeatures: Isolated cloud sandbox per thread with your repository and project setup
Agents run tests and checks before handing work back
Browser checks against a live preview of the running app
Opens GitHub pull requests that the workspace can review and steer
Start work from Slack, Linear, iMessage or Sentry, or from schedules, GitHub CI events and webhooks
CLI for macOS and Linux and an MCP server at api.hoplite.sh/mcp
bestFor: Startups and product teams that want cloud agents to verify changes in the running app and return reviewable PRs with evidence.
notIdealFor: Teams that want to run Claude Code or Codex harnesses unchanged, since Hoplite uses its own agent harness, or teams outside GitHub.
recentUpdates: Hoplite launched on Launch YC on July 30, 2026, and has since added automations triggered by GitHub, Sentry, Linear, Slack, schedules and webhooks, plus a Slack agent that answers code questions and opens coding threads.
verdict: A capable cloud agent product with strong verification and review tooling, best suited to GitHub teams that value product-level QA over raw code output.

name: Replicas
pricingDetail: Free trial with $100 of usage and no card required. Developer costs $50 per month including $50 of usage; Team costs $200 per month and up, in $100 steps, with usage equal to the price; Enterprise is custom. Workspaces bill per minute by size, from $0.004 per minute for 2 vCPU and 8 GB included, and model usage runs on your own subscriptions or API keys.
description: Replicas is a cloud coding-agent platform for engineering teams. It runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi or Muse Code in isolated Linux VMs that clone your code and dependencies, started from Linear, Slack, GitHub, GitLab, the dashboard, automations or the API, and returns pull requests, replies and recordings.
keyFeatures: Choice of agent harness per task: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi or Muse Code
Isolated Linux VM per task with configured environments, warm hooks, MCPs, skills and variables
Agents drive a desktop and browser and return screenshots and screen recordings
Reacts to PR comments, code reviews and CI failures
Previews of services running in the workspace
Automations, warm pools, API access and a mobile app
bestFor: Engineering teams that want background agents across several harnesses with full control over the environment each one runs in.
notIdealFor: Individual developers who want a free tier beyond the trial, or teams that want model usage bundled into one bill.
recentUpdates: Replicas, backed by Y Combinator (P26), now supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and Muse Code harnesses, with auto-sized workspaces and per-minute billing on Developer and Team plans.
verdict: A flexible, harness-agnostic background agent platform with clear usage pricing and strong environment controls.

name: Tembo
pricingDetail: 7-day free trial of Max. Pro costs $60 per month with $90 of monthly usage for up to 5 users; Max costs $200 per month with $400 of monthly usage for up to 10 users; Enterprise is custom. The allowance covers Tembo Gateway model usage and cloud VM compute; your own keys or Claude, Codex or SuperGrok subscriptions add no inference cost.
description: Tembo is an agent orchestration platform that runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Amp, OpenCode, Pi and other agents in isolated cloud VMs with the full product stack. Sessions include a terminal, workspace files, a live computer and public preview links, and can be triggered from issue trackers, chat and monitoring tools.
keyFeatures: Harness-agnostic orchestration of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Amp, OpenCode, Pi and custom agents
Isolated cloud VM per session with services, browser and graphical apps
Tembo Previews expose frontends and APIs through public links
Triggers from GitHub, Linear, Jira, Slack, Sentry, PagerDuty, schedules and webhooks
Hands-on live sessions that can be paused, shared or handed off to a background agent
BYOK for Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI, cloud BYOK for AWS Bedrock and GCP Vertex AI, and Claude, Codex or SuperGrok subscriptions
bestFor: Teams that want background agents to build and verify full-stack changes with running previews, triggered from the tools they already use.
notIdealFor: Solo developers who want a free plan after the trial, or teams that only need simple code edits without full environments.
recentUpdates: Tembo now positions itself around cloud coding agents with full environments and previews, offering Pro and Max plans with dollar-denominated usage allowances and VM compute metered by the second.
verdict: A broad, well-integrated platform for running any coding agent in complete cloud environments, strongest for teams that need previews and many integrations.

name: Vorflux
pricingDetail: Pay-as-you-go from prepaid credits with no per-seat price: bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Google keys, buy Vorflux tokens at standard provider rates with no platform fee (launch offer), or use a Codex subscription for GPT models. Server compute costs $0.2117 per hour for 2 vCPU and 8 GiB up to $3.3868 per hour for 32 vCPU and 128 GiB, and servers stop after 1 hour idle.
description: Vorflux is a cloud AI coding agent for teams that works from Slack. It plans each task, builds it on its own cloud machine with planner, builder, reviewer and QA sub-agents across several model providers, tests it and hands back a pull request with code, tests and evidence.
keyFeatures: Planner, builder, reviewer and QA sub-agents across Claude, GPT and Gemini models
Runs your repos and services, such as Docker Compose stacks and test suites, on a dedicated cloud machine
Returns PRs with tests, screenshots or recordings as evidence
AutoBots with a standing role, daily and weekly budgets and their own Slack channel
PR review with merge risk scores
Scheduled and event-triggered work from connected tools
bestFor: Teams that want an autonomous agent working from Slack and tickets, with tested PRs and risk-scored review.
notIdealFor: Developers who want a free plan or to steer agents in an editor, since Vorflux is billed per use and centred on Slack.
recentUpdates: Vorflux, founded in 2026 by Prasanna Sankar with Anant Nag and Haritha Elango, is in Y Combinator's Fall 2026 batch; it launched an MCP server in October 2026 and now ships 14 AutoBot templates and PR risk scoring.
verdict: An ambitious team-focused coding agent with strong verification and multi-model review, priced by usage with no token markup.

name: Open Session
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the MIT license. You self-host the server and pay only for your own hardware, sandbox providers and model subscriptions or API keys.
description: Open Session is an open-source, self-hosted control room for coding agents built by the team at Tella. A server with a web UI and Slack, Linear, Plain and GitHub agents runs coding sessions through the Pi engine in git worktrees on your own machine or in isolated sandboxes, with multiplayer sessions and review that ends in a pull request.
keyFeatures: Self-hosted server: checkouts, transcripts and keys stay on your hardware
Each session gets its own git worktree and branch for parallel agents
Multiplayer sessions shared as links with live presence
Sub-agents, automations from schedules, webhooks and watched channels
Worktree terminals, branch previews and PR review beside the transcript
Supports multiple Codex and Claude subscriptions and model APIs
bestFor: Teams that want a self-hosted, forkable agent orchestrator with Slack, Linear and GitHub intake and full control over data.
notIdealFor: Teams that want a managed SaaS without running a server, or users who need hardened authentication out of the box, since sign-in is opt-in.
recentUpdates: The tellahq/opensession repository, created in June 2026, is active with commits on November 9, 2026 and over 400 GitHub stars.
verdict: A capable open-source alternative to hosted agent platforms for teams willing to run their own server.

name: Nuphos
pricingDetail: Free for up to 3 members and 1 environment with 7 days of audit retention. Dev costs $29 per month, Team $99 per month with unlimited members, Business $299 per month and Scale $999 per month. Model usage runs on your own Claude or ChatGPT account, and cloud computers are billed on a separate team computer plan.
description: Nuphos is an open-source shared DevOps workspace for the coding agents a team already uses. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Grok Build or Antigravity run as runtimes on a managed cloud computer or your own machine, and teammates can join live sessions, share skills, tools and memory, and operate across AWS, GCP and Kubernetes with short-lived credentials and approvals.
keyFeatures: Runtimes for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Grok Build and Antigravity that keep their native harness
Agents keep working on a cloud computer or remote machine, with desktop, iOS and CLI clients
Shared live sessions where several people steer the same agent
Team-wide skills, tools and memory
Built-in Kubernetes, Grafana, GitHub, Linear and cloud consoles with short-lived credentials
Slack and Discord bots, schedule and webhook triggers, and an audit trail
bestFor: DevOps and platform teams that want to run coding agents together across infrastructure with approvals and audit logs.
notIdealFor: Solo developers who only need a local coding agent, or teams that need a mature product, since Nuphos is in early access.
recentUpdates: Desktop v0.112.0, released on November 9, 2026, lets owners answer nested agents' questions in a Bot's chat and reduces background polling and error reports.
verdict: A promising open-source team workspace for agent-driven operations work, still evolving quickly in early access.
